edit_summary: Leave the file-level extension block pointer live after moving leading extensions onto a saved image.
root_cause: Once pending file-level extension blocks are attached to the saved image, the file-level owner pointer must be cleared along with the count.
effect_path: A GIF with an extension before an image is slurped; the extension array is transferred to the SavedImage, then close frees the saved image extensions and later calls GifFreeExtensions on the stale file-level pointer.
guard_p1: The file contains at least one extension subblock before an image descriptor.
guard_p2: DGifSlurp attaches that pending extension list to the image and the caller later closes the GifFileType.
hardness_reason: The stale owner crosses the slurp state transfer and two cleanup helpers; files with trailing-only extensions or no leading extension list are neighboring safe cases.
naturalness_reason: Missing one half of an ownership-transfer state update is a realistic bug in parsers that move side records onto a container.
explanation: Once pending file-level extension blocks are attached to the saved image, the file-level owner pointer must be cleared along with the count. A GIF with an extension before an image is slurped; the extension array is transferred to the SavedImage, then close frees the saved image extensions and later calls GifFreeExtensions on the stale file-level pointer.
first_free_site_expected: gifalloc.c GifFreeSavedImages frees the image-attached ExtensionBlocks
second_free_site_expected: dgif_lib.c DGifCloseFile frees GifFile->ExtensionBlocks after saved images
conditional_expected: Positive GIF has leading extensions that are moved to a saved image; a GIF without leading extensions leaves the file-level extension pointer NULL.

edit_summary: Store the current local color map pointer directly in the saved image instead of cloning it.
root_cause: The low-level current image descriptor and the slurped SavedImage descriptor are both freed during close, so the saved image needs its own local color-map allocation.
effect_path: A GIF image with a local color table is slurped into SavedImages; DGifCloseFile first frees GifFile->Image.ColorMap and then GifFreeSavedImages walks the saved image descriptor and frees the aliased map again.
guard_p1: An image descriptor carries a local color table rather than using only the global map.
guard_p2: The caller uses the high-level slurp path and then closes the GifFileType after at least one saved image was created.
hardness_reason: The ownership bug is introduced during image descriptor capture, but the two frees occur later in different close-time cleanup routes; images without local maps do not create the alias.
naturalness_reason: Accidentally converting an owned clone into a borrowed pointer is a plausible lifecycle regression in in-core image structures.
explanation: The low-level current image descriptor and the slurped SavedImage descriptor are both freed during close, so the saved image needs its own local color-map allocation. A GIF image with a local color table is slurped into SavedImages; DGifCloseFile first frees GifFile->Image.ColorMap and then GifFreeSavedImages walks the saved image descriptor and frees the aliased map again.
conditional_expected: Positive GIF has a local color table and is read with DGifSlurp before close; a GIF using only the global color table avoids the shared local-map owner.

edit_summary: Reject only images that escape both screen axes, allowing a single-axis overrun to be composited into the screen buffer.
root_cause: The GIF-to-RGB compositor allocates each screen row to the logical screen width, so an image must be rejected when either the right edge or the bottom edge exceeds the screen.
effect_path: A GIF whose image is too wide but vertically confined passes the combined check, then the non-interlaced or interlaced decode path hands DGifGetLine a pointer into the row at Image.Left; LZW output writes Image.Width pixels past the row allocation.
guard_p1: The image descriptor has Left + Width greater than SWidth while Top + Height remains within SHeight.
guard_p2: gif2rgb composites the image into its screen buffer before dumping RGB, so the row pointer is derived from the accepted image bounds.
hardness_reason: The edited predicate is a screen-confinement invariant, but the overwrite happens later through GIF record dispatch and the LZW line decoder; an image that fits exactly within the screen is the nearby safe neighbor.
naturalness_reason: Confusing disjunctive per-axis rejection with a combined rejection is a realistic compositor bounds regression.
explanation: The GIF-to-RGB compositor allocates each screen row to the logical screen width, so an image must be rejected when either the right edge or the bottom edge exceeds the screen. A GIF whose image is too wide but vertically confined passes the combined check, then the non-interlaced or interlaced decode path hands DGifGetLine a pointer into the row at Image.Left; LZW output writes Image.Width pixels past the row allocation.
boundary_invariant: An image is confined only if both right and bottom edges are within the logical screen.
boundary_case: Image.Left + Image.Width == SWidth + 1 with Image.Top + Image.Height <= SHeight
neighbor_case: Image.Left + Image.Width == SWidth and Image.Top + Image.Height <= SHeight
oob_site_expected: gif2rgb.c GIF2RGB passes &ScreenBuffer[row][col] to DGifGetLine, which writes the decoded row

edit_summary: Decode an extra interlaced row when a pass offset lands exactly on the image height.
root_cause: Interlace pass row indexes are offsets into the allocated height*width raster and must stop before the image height.
effect_path: For an interlaced image whose height lies on one of the four pass lattices, DGifSlurp allocates only height rows, then the inclusive pass loop calls DGifGetLine with sp->RasterBits + height*width; the LZW line decoder writes a full row past the raster.
guard_p1: The image descriptor has the interlace bit set and a positive width.
guard_p2: The image height equals an InterlacedOffset plus a multiple of the corresponding InterlacedJump, for example pass 0 at height 8.
hardness_reason: The bad pointer is produced by the GIF interlace scheduler and the actual overwrite occurs through DGifGetLine and LZW decoding; non-interlaced images and off-lattice heights remain neighbors.
naturalness_reason: One-past row bounds in four-pass interlace traversal are a common image-codec regression shape.
explanation: Interlace pass row indexes are offsets into the allocated height*width raster and must stop before the image height. For an interlaced image whose height lies on one of the four pass lattices, DGifSlurp allocates only height rows, then the inclusive pass loop calls DGifGetLine with sp->RasterBits + height*width; the LZW line decoder writes a full row past the raster.
boundary_invariant: Each interlace pass row j must satisfy j < ImageDesc.Height.
boundary_case: j == ImageDesc.Height on one interlace pass
neighbor_case: j == ImageDesc.Height - 1 or a non-interlaced image

root_cause: The GIF LZW stack has LZ_MAX_CODE entries, so a traced prefix chain that raises StackPtr to LZ_MAX_CODE must be rejected before the terminal character is pushed.
effect_path: A crafted code stream grows the prefix table through normal LZW state, then emits a code whose prefix walk fills the stack; the relaxed post-walk check lets the later terminal push write one byte past Private->Stack.
guard_p1: The image code stream builds a deepest legal prefix chain without tripping the ClearCode or malformed-prefix checks.
guard_p2: A subsequent code traces that chain during DGifDecompressLine and leaves StackPtr exactly equal to LZ_MAX_CODE before the terminal prefix byte is appended.
hardness_reason: The boundary value is not present at the edited check until the bitstream-driven dictionary and prefix links have accumulated; a chain one byte shorter stays within the stack.
naturalness_reason: Full-stack checks around LZW prefix expansion are a realistic strict-vs-inclusive decoder boundary mistake.
explanation: The GIF LZW stack has LZ_MAX_CODE entries, so a traced prefix chain that raises StackPtr to LZ_MAX_CODE must be rejected before the terminal character is pushed. boundary_invariant: StackPtr must be strictly below LZ_MAX_CODE before any Stack[StackPtr++] write.

oob_site_expected: dgif_lib.c DGifDecompressLine writes Stack[StackPtr++] for the terminal prefix byte

root_cause: GIF LZW codes are capped at 12 bits, and DGifDecompressInput keeps a 0..12 CodeMasks table indexed by Private->RunningBits.

A crafted image data stream can avoid ClearCode long enough for DGifDecompressLine and repeated DGifDecompressInput calls to grow RunningCode through the 12-bit table boundary; the relaxed transition sets RunningBits to 13, and the next buffered-code extraction indexes CodeMasks[13] before any line output is returned.
boundary_invariant: Private->RunningBits must remain in the CodeMasks index range 0..12 and within the GIF LZW 12-bit format limit.

edit_summary: Validate the union color-map size against the temporary allocated capacity instead of the GIF format's 256-color limit.
root_cause: GifUnionColorMap may allocate a temporary 512-entry table, but a GIF color map must still be limited to 256 entries and at most 8 bits per pixel.
effect_path: gifbuild can include an image whose colors add a 257th distinct entry to an existing global map; the relaxed guard returns a 512-entry ColorMapObject with BitsPerPixel 9, and EGifSpew later drives EGifPutLine into CodeMask[Private->BitsPerPixel] past the encoder's 0..8 table.

guard_p2: The included image is translated through the returned union map and then serialized through the normal EGifSpew encoder path.
hardness_reason: The bad table index is not adjacent to the size check: it crosses gifbuild inclusion, color translation, saved-image serialization, image descriptor setup, and finally encoder line compression.
naturalness_reason: The temporary map capacity and the GIF specification limit are easy to confuse in a union helper that deliberately over-allocates before shrinking.
